tools.description: Runs the authority check and derives the install arguments itself, then reads the fee payer sequence and fees and records unsigned authorization to assemble bounded unsigned XDR. Never signs or submits. Recording mode does not enforce owner authorization: the wallet must independently validate all returned fields, recheck authority, obtain protected user approval, construct owner authorization and enforce-simulate before signing. A separate restoration response contains only a restore transaction and requires a fresh intent and assembly after execution. Uses only an operator-configured RPC source; may rebuild generated policies.

CheckPolicyCallSurfaceInput.description:
Network-read operation. The trusted acquisition shell resolves `rpc_source` from configured
endpoints for `network_id`, validates both against the spec and binding set, and acquires
the account code, rule state, policy and verifier code and ledger anchor itself. Clients
cannot supply those observations, and nothing about who owns the account is accepted from
them: the authority list is derived from the ledger (Decision D7).

rpc_source.description: Name of a configured RPC source, not an arbitrary client-provided URL.

rule_index.description:
The spec rule about to be installed. Its signers are the restricted keys the findings
look for, and its target is the contract they may call. An index into the hashed
spec, not a separate claim.

resolution_reference.description:
Deployment transaction hash or immutable registry reference used to resolve this
exact instance. Informational evidence; recognition is verified independently.

PolicyBindingSet.description: Exact deployed instances corresponding positionally to every PolicyRef in a spec.

fee_payer.description: Classic G-address paying the fee and sequence; no private key is accepted.

intent_request.description: Re-run this authority check. A caller-supplied intent or verdict is never accepted.

max_fee_stroops.description: Inclusive maximum fee for the one returned envelope, in stroops.

validity_ledgers.description: 1..=120 ledgers, measured from the sequence read. Not an authority validity window.

tools.name: assemble_install_transaction

registry_snapshot_root.description: Root of the verified signed snapshot used to recognize account and policy code.

summary.description:
The verdict in plain words, for a person: scope, refusals first, who can change the
account, what was not checked. Derived from `verdict`; never says "safe".

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error codes surfaced to agents (architecture §4.6). Kept
in one place so the whole toolkit shares one vocabulary; new codes are appended,
never renumbered.

oneOf.description:
A supplied recording's decoded views are not what the recorder derives from its
own raw evidence (or its schema/version is not current).

The builder could not be started or configured at all — a misconfigured
`stellar` binary path, an unusable build cache, a rejected operator setting.
Distinct from `EBuildFailed` so an operator fault is never reported to an agent
as "your spec does not compile".

Every build slot on a hosted server is in use. Retryable by design: the same request
can succeed once a running build finishes.

The caller cancelled the request (or its session ended) and the server stopped the
work: a build was terminated or a read stopped before its next RPC call. MCP sends the
cancelling client no response, so this is the outcome's name, not a wire answer to it.

The pinned root policy itself is unusable: malformed or weak keys, a threshold the keys
cannot meet, or the public development root configured for a network other than testnet.
An operator configuration fault, distinct from a snapshot whose signatures do not verify.

A rule that can change the account has a shape the authority check cannot describe
(a policy-guarded owner rule, a nested-account signer, an unrecognized verifier).
A restricted (delegate) key can already change the account on its own.

A restricted key already has another usable rule on the new rule's target, so a
stateful limit would not hold.

The record-mode simulation of a supported capture failed: the target refused the call
(for example an insufficient balance or a missing recipient), or the endpoint's
simulator failed, which its withheld text cannot distinguish. Not a transport fault.

The captured call's state is archived: a restoration preamble, a simulation that restored
archived entries, or a footprint entry archived or expiring at the captured ledger.
Capture never performs a restoration.

No local wallet bridge on this server (hosted MCP never has one), the wallet did not
answer, or its reply was not understood. Offer the manual install skill.

No usable connection: the pairing code was refused, or the connection expired, was
replaced or reached its delivery limit. The user selects Connect Claude for a fresh code.
The wallet is in the middle of another action. Retryable with identical input.
A different proposal from this session is still waiting for the user in the wallet.
The wallet refused the proposal's content. Reconnecting does not help.

A file name that is not a plain relative path inside the published directory: a `..` or
`.` component, an absolute path, a separator other than `/`, a symlink or a non-file.
The Wasm's SHA-256 is not the BuildManifest's `wasm_hash`, or not the directory's name.

The BuildManifest does not describe the supplied spec, crate source or lockfile, or is
not a BuildManifest of the current schema.

The published index does not list exactly the directory's files with their SHA-256, or
the directory is not the layout `publish-artifact` writes.

The destination already holds a published directory for this Wasm hash with other
content. Publishing identical content again succeeds.
The envelope ONLY restores entries. After execution, acquire and assemble a new intent.
Restoration is included by the protocol in the invocation's declared resources.

InstallOperation.description: The only account operation represented by a prepared install intent.

InstallPolicy.description: One address and its value in the account's `Map<Address, Val>` policy argument.

address.description: The exact deployed address from that binding.

policy_index.description: Position in the selected PolicySpec rule and its PolicyBindingSet.

InstallPolicyParams.description:
Account-install arguments for the policy kinds this toolkit composes. The assembler
encodes `Generated` as the generated policy's ignored `u32` value `0`. The spending
limit fields encode `SpendingLimitAccountParams` from the reviewed account library.

spending_limit.description: Canonical decimal i128 from the spec's reviewed `limit` parameter.

PolicyAuthorityEvidence.description:
How the state was acquired. Not part of the approval commitment — ledger numbers, TTLs and
endpoint metadata move without any change in authority — but every read was validated
against it (one endpoint ledger: one response, or for more than 200 keys several reporting
the same ledger; requested keys only; complete reconciliation).

evidence_trust.description: `rpc_reported`: as trustworthy as the configured endpoint, no ledger proof.

raw_ordered_entry_digest.description:
Digest of every raw entry the read used (keys, values, TTLs, absences); it moves with
every payment by a classic signer, which is why it is evidence and not the commitment.

source.description: The operator's name for the RPC source; never its URL.

expired_rules.description: Expired rules that would reach a protected surface or the target if revived.

restricted_key_rules.description: Every live rule, in any context, naming one of the restricted keys.

target_rules.description: Other rules on the target the agent cannot use alone: who else can call it.

PolicyAuthorityState.description: The authority-relevant state behind the answer; part of the commitment.

classic_accounts.description: Signing configuration of every classic account the answer consulted.

ordered_state_digest.description:
Canonical hash of the ordered account rules and transitive storage entries, with every
installed policy's observed code hash. TTLs are not in it.

verifiers.description: Code of every verifier the answer consulted.

PolicyCallSurfaceVerdict.description:
Who could change the account, reset the bound policies, or call the new rule's target, at
one observed ledger, for the stated `scope` only. Never a safety verdict, and advisory to
whoever receives it over MCP: the wallet that holds the owner key recomputes it against its
own RPC and accepts only when `refusals` and `unresolved` are both empty and every
`authority_list` entry names at least one identity it trusts (its own keys, or identities
trusted through its protected UI, never one marked `aliases_restricted_key`) (Decision D7).

authority_commitment.description:
Hash of the separate canonical `CommitmentPreimage` in `ozpb-call-surface-core`,
documented in `docs/CANONICAL-HASHING.md`. It includes the registry snapshot root
and each bound policy's address/code observation, not just the verdict's addresses.
The observed ledger and acquisition evidence are excluded. Approval binds to this
hash and the pre-signing re-read recomputes it; it authenticates nothing by itself.

authority_list.description:
Every live rule that can change the account or reach a bound policy, as policy-free
`all_of` requirements over resolved identities, in rule order.

authority_state.description: The authority-relevant state behind the answer (committed).

coverage_exclusions.description: Live rules for other contracts: not analysed.

evidence.description: How the state was acquired (recorded, never compared).

grant.description: The spec rule the answer is about, with its exact `add_context_rule` arguments.

notes.description: Information for the screen; none of it blocks.

refusals.description: Unconditional refusals inside the scope. Trust never overrides one.

scope.description:
What the answer covers: the target(s), the account's management surface and the bound
policies. Never an account-wide "nothing else".

unresolved.description: Evidence gaps inside the scope. Any entry blocks acceptance.

PolicyGrant.description: The rule being installed, as the check read it from the hashed spec.

policies.description: The new rule's `policies` map, in spec order.

signers.description: The new rule's signers: the restricted keys the refusals look for.

stateful.description: The rule keeps state between calls (a counter or a spending window).

target.description: The contract the new `CallContract` rule targets.

PolicyIdentity.description:
A required identity with what a wallet compares against its own keys. One marked
`aliases_restricted_key` must never be counted as an owner.

oneOf.description: An existing classic Stellar account controlled by its master key alone.

A key behind a recognized owner verifier. Match on `scheme` + `public_key` (the
canonical key); the verifier address is only where this account checks it, and the
same key behind another copy of that verifier is the same identity. An ed25519 key here
is also the same identity as a classic account whose master key it is.

public_key.description: Canonical key, hex: 32 bytes for ed25519, the first 65 bytes for WebAuthn.

oneOf.description: A `Default` rule: every call the account authorizes, management included.
`CallContract(account)`: the account's own management methods.
`CallContract(bound policy)`: that policy's install/uninstall, which resets its state.
`CallContract(target)`: a second way to call the new rule's target.

PolicyRequirement.description: Who must sign for the rule to authorize anything.

oneOf.description: A policy-free rule: every one of these must sign.

Every policy is recognized as demanding at least one of the rule's own signers: any
one of these, within those policies' further limits.

usable_alone.description: The restricted keys can use the rule without anyone else.

PolicyRuleEnumerationEvidence.description:
Only complete enumeration strategies can produce a verdict. The reader must verify
the active count and resolve every rule's transitive signer and policy references.

PolicySignerKey.description: A signer exactly as the account stores it.

rule_id.description: `null` when the finding is about the new rule itself; never omitted.

unsupported.description: Which shape this version refuses, on `E_UNSUPPORTED_AUTHORITY`.

oneOf.description:
A policy decides who may act: any policy on a rule that can change the account or reach
a bound policy (a k-of-n threshold, a guarded recovery rule), or an unreadable one.
A contract signer (nested smart account).
An external signer whose verifier is not recognized.
A classic account with other signers or thresholds the master key cannot meet.
A classic account that does not exist, so cannot authenticate now.
Key data a recognized verifier can never accept.

PolicyVerifierObservation.description:
The code observed at a verifier, and its scheme when that code is a recognized owner
verifier.

PrepareInstallIntentOutput.description:
The install intent: the exact `add_context_rule` arguments, derived from the same `grant`
the authority answer's commitment covers, offered only when that answer has no refusal and
nothing unresolved. It is NOT a signed or even assembled transaction — assembling one needs
current sequence, fees, ledger bounds and restoration preambles (wallet-owned) — and NOT a
safety verdict: the wallet holding the owner key recomputes the answer, matches the listed
owners, and signs only on the user's confirmation (§6.2, Decision D7).

account_contract.description: The smart-account contract on which `add_context_rule` is invoked.

authority.description:
The live authority answer these arguments were checked against; its
`authority_commitment` covers them.

context_contract.description: The contract named by the new rule's `CallContract` context.

delegate_signers.description:
The account's typed signer arguments for `add_context_rule`, in the same shape the
authority answer reports them.

policies.description:
One entry per policy in the selected spec rule. The preparer must match each
index and address to the binding set, match the install parameters to the spec,
and reject missing or duplicate indexes and addresses before returning an intent.

valid_until_ledger.description: Explicit `null` means no expiration; omission must not silently grant one.

envelope_xdr_sha256.description: SHA-256 of envelope bytes, not the Stellar network transaction hash.

sequence_read_ledger.description: These reads are separately labeled; they are not one atomic ledger snapshot.

simulation_auth_mode.description: Always `record`: no owner authorization was enforced by this simulation.

source_sequence.description: The payer's observed sequence, before the +1 used in this envelope.

writes_committed.description: Always false. This tool never submits anything.

tools.description: Read-only, state-dependent network read through an operator-configured RPC source (the request names the source and network; it never carries a URL). Takes one unsigned envelope with no authorization entries whose only call is a native Stellar Asset Contract transfer(contract account, existing G recipient, positive amount) on that network, and returns its target capture: the ledger header, state-archival configuration, the call, the account's executed Wasm hash and every footprint entry at one ledger, provenance rpc_reported (an endpoint's answer, not an inclusion proof). The record-mode simulation it uses is acquisition only, never evidence that a policy permits the call. Any other target, function or envelope shape is refused (E_UNSUPPORTED_ENVELOPE). The envelope is confidential input: it reaches the configured RPC endpoint and this conversation, and no result or error echoes it; the capture repeats its call (account, recipient, amount) and is equally confidential. Prefer the CLI or a local stdio server. The output is the capture the native worker's captured-target modes read; this tool does not run the captured-target layer, signs nothing and submits nothing.

envelope_xdr_base64.description:
Unsigned transaction envelope, canonical base64 XDR, with no authorization entries.
Confidential input (§6.5): it reaches the configured RPC endpoint (and, over MCP, the
conversation and server that carry the request), and is never echoed in a result, an
error or this type's `Debug` output. The result repeats its call, so it is confidential
too.

network_id.description: Hex network ID; the named source must be configured for exactly this network.

rpc_source.description: Name of an operator-configured RPC source. The request never carries a URL.

tools.name: capture_target

data_xdr.description: Canonical `LedgerEntryData` XDR; the outer `LedgerEntry` extension is not captured.

live_until_ledger.description: Present for contract data and code.

account_code_hash.description: Lowercase hex Wasm hash the account instance executed at `observed_ledger`.

invocation_xdr.description: Canonical `InvokeContractArgs` XDR of the captured call, with no authorization.

network_id.description: Hex network ID of the source network.

observed_ledger.description: The ledger the simulation and the entry read both reported.

provenance.description: Always `rpc_reported`: an endpoint's answer, not an inclusion proof.

read_only_keys.description: Read-only footprint keys (canonical `LedgerKey` XDR), excluding the account's own.

read_write_keys.description: Read-write footprint keys (canonical `LedgerKey` XDR), excluding the account's own.

recording_auth_xdr.description: Record-mode authorization entry XDR. Discovery only; never evidence of enforcement.

state_archival.description: The network's state-archival configuration entry at `observed_ledger`.

tools.description: State-dependent prediction for one explicitly selected installed rule, through an operator-configured RPC source. Recognizes exact reviewed code or locally reproduced generated artifacts and reads rule, signers, policies, counters, configuration and TTLs at one reported ledger/hash. Candidate signer identities MUST successfully authenticate later; this tool does not verify signatures. A foreign candidate signer denies. Unknown implementations, unavailable/archived state and unmodeled authentication return unsupported. Results contain exact observations and require a fresh check plus enforce simulation of the actual authorization before signing. This is not an account safety or ownership verdict and never signs, restores or submits. May rebuild generated policies.

resolution_reference.description:
Deployment transaction hash or immutable registry reference used to resolve this
exact instance. Informational evidence; recognition is verified independently.

PolicyBindingSet.description: Exact deployed instances corresponding positionally to every PolicyRef in a spec.

PolicyCheckSigner.description:
Signer identities proposed for a policy check. The current verifier implementation
hash is an observation, so an external signer cannot supply it here.

account_address.description: Smart account whose installed rule and policy state will be read.

candidate_signers.description:
Candidate signer identities for this authorization. The server reads live rule
signers, verifier code, counters and ledger state from the selected network.

installed_context_rule_id.description:
On-chain context-rule ID selected for this check, not a claim about its state.
The server must read the rule at the observation ledger, verify its context,
validity and policy addresses against the selected spec rule and binding set,
then evaluate its live signers under the spec's authorization semantics. A missing
or mismatched rule cannot produce a permit. Never infer this ID from `rule_index`.

invocation.description: Proposed invocation, not an observation of installed policy state.

network_id.description: Must match the spec and binding set; the server selects a configured endpoint.

rpc_source.description: Name of a configured RPC source, never an arbitrary client URL.

rule_index.description: Index of the policy rule in `spec`; this is not an on-chain rule ID.

spec.description:
PolicySpec and exact installed instance bindings. Recognition is verified by the
toolkit; there is deliberately no caller-supplied `recognized` boolean.

tools.name: check_against_policy

account_address.description:
Request identities. A consumer must compare these to the original request and
independently verify the trusted server's response before relying on a prediction.

classic_account_reads.description: Classic accounts have no TTL and are never encoded as contract-data observations.

configuration_reads.description:
Exact XDR key/value pairs and TTLs used to resolve the selected account rule,
its signers and policies, and the policies' own configuration.

installed_context_rule_id.description:
The on-chain rule whose signer set and policy state were read. The wallet must
select this same rule when authorizing the eventual transaction.

observed_ledger.description: Ledger at which every storage and configuration entry below was read.

recheck_before_signing.description:
State may change immediately after this observation. A new live check is needed
immediately before a transaction is signed; this is not a validity interval.

registry_snapshot_root.description: Root of the verified registry snapshot used to recognize policy implementations.

request_hash.description:
Domain-separated canonical hash of the full [`CheckAgainstPolicyInput`], including
the invocation and ordered candidate-signer identities. The server computes this
via [`CheckAgainstPolicyInput::request_hash`]; it never accepts a caller claim.

spec_hash.description: Hash of the validated PolicySpec and exact PolicyBindingSet used for this check.

storage_reads.description: Exact XDR key/value pairs and TTLs used to evaluate installed policy state.

value_xdr_base64.description: Canonical Account LedgerEntryData XDR; None records endpoint omission.

PolicyStateObservation.description:
A missing key is a real observation, not a missing field. A present entry always
carries both the XDR value and its TTL, so incomplete evidence cannot claim either.

value_xdr_base64.description: Canonical full LedgerEntryData XDR, including its embedded key identity.

observation.description: A checked absence or the exact value and TTL observed at the ledger anchor.

oneOf.description: Required persistence was omitted: it may never have existed or be archived.

refusal_required.description: True for an adapter-required or refuse-on-drift identity.

RecheckBeforeSigning.description: A prediction always requires a fresh live check immediately before signing.

evidence.description: Present only when a complete endpoint observation was acquired.

tools.description: Advisory, state-dependent network read through an operator-configured RPC source. For one spec rule about to be installed, lists every live rule that can change the account or reset the bound policies, each with exactly who must sign (authority_list), plus refusals (authority already unacceptable, or shapes this version does not support), unresolved evidence gaps, other rules on the target, rules for other contracts that were not analysed, and an authority_commitment over the state and the exact install arguments. It never says an account is safe and never decides who the owners are: only the wallet that holds the owner key can, after recomputing this itself. Tell the user to confirm it there. `summary` is the plain-words reading. May rebuild generated policies to recognize them before reading.

A contract signer (nested smart account).
An external signer whose verifier is not recognized.
A classic account with other signers or thresholds the master key cannot meet.
A classic account that does not exist, so cannot authenticate now.
Key data a recognized verifier can never accept.

PolicyVerifierObservation.description:
The code observed at a verifier, and its scheme when that code is a recognized owner
verifier.

registry_snapshot_root.description: Root of the verified signed snapshot used to recognize account and policy code.

summary.description:
The verdict in plain words, for a person: scope, refusals first, who can change the
account, what was not checked. Derived from `verdict`; never says "safe".

tools.description: Pair with the user's same-machine testnet wallet using the one-time code its Connect Claude button shows. Returns public account, delegate and limits. No signing or installation authority. Unavailable on hosted MCP.
tools.name: connect_wallet

tools.description: Evaluate whether a candidate invocation would be permitted under a PolicySpec, using the independent reference evaluator. Pure; returns permit or deny + machine-readable reason.
tools.name: evaluate_spec

deny_reason.description:
Present on deny or indeterminate: the machine-readable reason. The wire name is retained
for compatibility even though an indeterminate reason is not a denial.

verdict.description:
"permit", "deny", or "indeterminate". The last verdict is fail-closed: at least one
composed reviewed policy is outside the Phase 1 evaluator's model.

tools.description: Generate and build the deterministic, immutable Stellar smart-contract policy artifact for a PolicySpec rule: locked Rust source, Wasm, and a binding BuildManifest. Resource-consuming; never deploys or signs.
tools.name: generate_code

build_manifest.description: BuildManifest binding the spec/codegen/source/lock/toolchain/Wasm artifact chain.

files.description: Relative path → file contents (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/contract.rs, …).

normalized_input_hash.description: Pre-build normalized codegen input hash (hex). NOT the wasm hash (§4.10).

soroban_sdk_version.description: Pinned build inputs recorded for the BuildManifest.

wasm_base64.description: Built Wasm bytes. This is base64 to keep the JSON/MCP artifact self-contained.

tools.description: Record from a self-contained raw-XDR evidence bundle (offline). Pure; carries self_supplied trust (internally consistent but not network-verified) when the transaction result XDR is supplied and agrees with the claimed outcome, incomplete without it.

result_xdr_base64.description:
Raw `TransactionResult` XDR; checked against `successful` when recording. Without
it the import is labeled `incomplete` and cannot drive synthesis.

successful.description:
Supplier claim that the transaction succeeded (verified against
`result_xdr_base64` when recording).

tools.name: import_recording

tools.description: Simulate one exact envelope, including any intended authorization entries, through Stellar RPC with authorization enforced. Returns the endpoint-reported outcome (simulated_success, simulation_failed, restoration_required, or declared_resources_insufficient naming each footprint list that is not exactly the simulated one and each disk-read or write limit below the use) and ledger for that exact envelope. below_endpoint_estimate is advice: declared instructions or resource fee below the endpoint's padded estimate, which never changes the outcome. State-dependent; writes are discarded. Does not identify an installed policy or submit a transaction. Signed authorization entries are live authorizations: anyone who sees the envelope can submit them until their signatureExpirationLedger, and simulation does not consume their nonce. The envelope reaches the RPC endpoint and this conversation; prefer testnet or a short expiration and a trusted endpoint. A hosted server refuses signed envelopes; use the CLI or a local stdio server.
tools.name: preflight_transaction

PreflightDeclaredResource.description:
A part of the envelope's declared Soroban transaction data that must match the simulated
one, which the endpoint reports as used, without padding. An envelope without Soroban
transaction data declares an empty footprint and zero limits.

oneOf.description:
The declared read-only list is not exactly the simulated one, in any order: a key is
missing, extra, or repeated. Extra keys are not harmless: the network charges for the
declared footprint.
The declared read-write list is not exactly the simulated one, in any order.
The declared disk-read bytes are below the simulated use.
The declared write bytes are below the simulated use.

PreflightEstimatedResource.description:
A declared value below the endpoint's own padded estimate for it. Advice only, because the
endpoint reports these padded rather than as used.

oneOf.description: Below the endpoint's recommended instruction budget, which pads the simulated use.

Below the endpoint's resource fee estimate, priced from padded resources at its
reported ledger's rates.

The invocation succeeded at the endpoint's state. The envelope declares exactly the
simulated footprint and at least the simulated disk-read and write bytes; its
instructions and resource fee are not established.

The endpoint reported an error after reading its ledger: an invocation or authorization
failure, or an error inside its simulator. The endpoint's text is withheld because it
can echo the envelope. A refusal before the endpoint read its ledger is an error.

Success needed archived entries restored first, whether by a separate restoration
preamble or inside the simulation. It is not a success against current state.

The invocation succeeded in simulation, but in each listed dimension the envelope as
written does not declare what the simulation used, so the simulation does not show that
the envelope can succeed.

auth_mode.description: `enforce`, as opposed to recording authorization without enforcing it.

below_endpoint_estimate.description:
Advice only: declared values below the endpoint's padded estimate, compared only after
a simulated success (`simulated_success` or `declared_resources_insufficient`) and empty
otherwise. It never changes `outcome`: a declaration below an estimate can still cover
the use, and one above it can still fall short at the network's rates.

envelope_xdr_sha256.description:
SHA-256 of canonical envelope XDR bytes, not a transaction hash. The endpoint received
exactly these bytes, base64-encoded.

evidence_trust.description: `rpc_reported`; the endpoint supplies the simulation result.

insufficient_declared_resources.description:
Each declared Soroban resource that does not match what the simulation used. Non-empty
exactly when `outcome` is `declared_resources_insufficient`. Footprint keys are not
named: they are confidential envelope content.

reported_ledger.description: Ledger sequence as reported by the selected RPC endpoint.

state_dependent.description: Always true for a live RPC simulation.

tools.description: Recognize candidate bindings and reproduce its artifact, derive the selected-rule reference suite, and bind the complete request to a run hash. Account-Wasm, captured-target and live-enforcement execution are explicitly unavailable; complete is false. Resource-consuming, no network reads, signing or submission. This is not the full dry_run.

CheckPolicyCallSurfaceInput.description:
Network-read operation. The trusted acquisition shell resolves `rpc_source` from configured
endpoints for `network_id`, validates both against the spec and binding set, and acquires
the account code, rule state, policy and verifier code and ledger anchor itself. Clients
cannot supply those observations, and nothing about who owns the account is accepted from
them: the authority list is derived from the ledger (Decision D7).

rpc_source.description: Name of a configured RPC source, not an arbitrary client-provided URL.

rule_index.description:
The spec rule about to be installed. Its signers are the restricted keys the findings
look for, and its target is the contract they may call. An index into the hashed
spec, not a separate claim.

resolution_reference.description:
Deployment transaction hash or immutable registry reference used to resolve this
exact instance. Informational evidence; recognition is verified independently.

PolicyBindingSet.description: Exact deployed instances corresponding positionally to every PolicyRef in a spec.

claimed_build_manifest.description: BuildManifest supplied with the artifact. Omission is reported separately.

claimed_generated_files.description:
Every generated file except `Cargo.lock`, as relative path → contents. This is
exactly the set hashed into `source_hash`: it includes `Cargo.toml`,
`rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, and `src/contract.rs`.

The implementation must compare the complete key set as well as contents. A missing
manifest/toolchain file or an extra source module is a mismatch, not reproduction.

claimed_wasm_base64.description: Built artifact to reproduce. Omission is reported as not verified, never success.

generated_artifact.description:
Instead of the three claimed fields: the `build_manifest_hash` that `generate_code`
returned earlier in the same MCP session. That server substitutes the files, Wasm and
manifest it built before anything is checked or hashed, so the request is evaluated
exactly as if they had been sent — without copying a crate and its Wasm through the
conversation. Every other entry point refuses it.

artifact.description: Claimed source, Wasm and manifest for exactly the candidate's spec and rule.

candidate.description:
Exact candidate identities and operator RPC source name. This is input to
recognition, not a caller-provided authority verdict or ledger observation.

candidate_context_rule_id.description:
Proposed chain ID, independent of the spec index. A later live execution
must read and check the actual NextId; this field is not proof of that ID.

run_nonce.description: Canonical lowercase 32-byte hex nonce to distinguish otherwise identical runs.

tools.name: prepare_dry_run

DryRunAcceptance.description:
Whether the executed evidence meets the permit/deny bar: the original call permitted, and
enough derived denials reverted in executed Wasm. Counted only from layers that passed.

executed_layers.description: One entry per layer this run executed, in layer order.

meets_minimum.description:
The reference layer passed, `original_permitted` holds, and one executed layer
reverted at least `required_reverted_denials` derived denials.

original_permitted.description: At least one layer executed, and every executed layer passed and permitted the original.

required_reverted_denials.description: Fewest derived denials one executed layer must revert.

account_code_hash.description: Registry-recognized spec identity, not a live code observation.

policy_code_hashes.description:
Exact contract-address → reproduced/recognized Wasm hash for every binding.
This is not proof of the current contents of those deployed addresses.

agree.description:
Recomputed by the coordinator: the outcome equals the expectation, and a refusal is the
error its class predicts, raised by the contract that owns that error, with state
unchanged. The worker's own verdict is necessary, never sufficient.

class.description: The reference case's mutation class in snake case, e.g. `arg_equality`.

expected_permit.description: The preparation's expectation for this case, not the worker's.

state_unchanged.description: Local state was identical before and after the call.

DryRunEnforcer.description: The contract that raised an attributed refusal, by its role in the candidate grant.

execution.description:
Present only on a layer this run executed, once the worker's report was bound to the
preparation: the identities it ran under and every case, each re-checked against the
preparation's expectation. Never present in a preparation, and never on a layer whose
report was refused.

reason.description: Stable explanation of the actual evidence or missing prerequisite.

writes_committed.description:
Writes committed to a live network. No layer here commits one. An offline layer's
permitted calls commit only fresh synthetic local state, which its `execution`
provenance states.

original_permitted.description: The layer passed and permitted its original call.

reverted_denials.description:
Derived denials this layer refused with the predicted error and unchanged state; zero
unless the layer passed.

DryRunLayerExecution.description:
One executed layer's bound evidence. The offline binding equals the one derived from the
preparation; `execution_network_id` is re-derived from it, never a live network.

controls.description: Signature, nonce, payload, rule-binding and replay controls (account-Wasm layer only).

execution_network_id.description: Counterfactual network the layer executed in, derived from the binding above.

stateful.description: The call-cap sequence, when the selected rule has a cap (account-Wasm layer only).

VerifyOutput.description:
Each dimension is reported separately — never collapsed into one "pure" boolean
(architecture §6.3). Live preflight remains state-dependent and separate.

models_all_policies.description:
Whether layer 1 models **every** policy composed into this rule. Its own dimension,
deliberately not folded into `matches`: "the reproductions agree" and "the evidence
covers every composed policy" are different claims, and collapsing them would let a
green `matches` imply coverage the report does not have.

unmodeled_reviewed_policies.description:
The composed reviewed policies layer 1 does not model, as `"rule[<i>]: <kind>"`.
Non-empty means those policies are enforced only on-chain.

acceptance.description: Filled only by a coordinator that executed layers; absent from a preparation.

complete.description:
False until every required runtime layer is actually executed and checked.
This is never an account-safety or transaction-authorization verdict.

layers.description: Always the four named layers in their declared order.

reference_case_ledgers.description: Synthetic ledger for each selected reference outcome, in the same order.

reference_report.description: Selected-rule reference evidence only, with explicit model gaps.

run_hash.description: Canonical hash of the full typed request, including artifact claims and nonce.

tools.description: Runs check_policy_call_surface itself (same request, same operator-configured RPC source) and, only when it returns no refusal and nothing unresolved, returns the exact add_context_rule arguments derived from the grant its authority_commitment covers, with that answer attached. A refusal or an unresolved item is an error carrying every finding. Never says an account is safe, never assembles, signs or submits: the user's wallet recomputes the check, matches every listed owner to the user's own keys or trusted identities, and asks the user. May rebuild generated policies.

resolution_reference.description:
Deployment transaction hash or immutable registry reference used to resolve this
exact instance. Informational evidence; recognition is verified independently.

PolicyBindingSet.description: Exact deployed instances corresponding positionally to every PolicyRef in a spec.

rpc_source.description: Name of a configured RPC source, not an arbitrary client-provided URL.

rule_index.description:
The spec rule about to be installed. Its signers are the restricted keys the findings
look for, and its target is the contract they may call. An index into the hashed
spec, not a separate claim.

tools.name: prepare_install_intent

registry_snapshot_root.description: Root of the verified signed snapshot used to recognize account and policy code.

summary.description:
The verdict in plain words, for a person: scope, refusals first, who can change the
account, what was not checked. Derived from `verdict`; never says "safe".

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error codes surfaced to agents (architecture §4.6). Kept
in one place so the whole toolkit shares one vocabulary; new codes are appended,
never renumbered.

oneOf.description:
A supplied recording's decoded views are not what the recorder derives from its
own raw evidence (or its schema/version is not current).

The builder could not be started or configured at all — a misconfigured
`stellar` binary path, an unusable build cache, a rejected operator setting.
Distinct from `EBuildFailed` so an operator fault is never reported to an agent
as "your spec does not compile".

Every build slot on a hosted server is in use. Retryable by design: the same request
can succeed once a running build finishes.

The caller cancelled the request (or its session ended) and the server stopped the
work: a build was terminated or a read stopped before its next RPC call. MCP sends the
cancelling client no response, so this is the outcome's name, not a wire answer to it.

The pinned root policy itself is unusable: malformed or weak keys, a threshold the keys
cannot meet, or the public development root configured for a network other than testnet.
An operator configuration fault, distinct from a snapshot whose signatures do not verify.

A rule that can change the account has a shape the authority check cannot describe
(a policy-guarded owner rule, a nested-account signer, an unrecognized verifier).
A restricted (delegate) key can already change the account on its own.

A restricted key already has another usable rule on the new rule's target, so a
stateful limit would not hold.

The record-mode simulation of a supported capture failed: the target refused the call
(for example an insufficient balance or a missing recipient), or the endpoint's
simulator failed, which its withheld text cannot distinguish. Not a transport fault.

The captured call's state is archived: a restoration preamble, a simulation that restored
archived entries, or a footprint entry archived or expiring at the captured ledger.
Capture never performs a restoration.

No local wallet bridge on this server (hosted MCP never has one), the wallet did not
answer, or its reply was not understood. Offer the manual install skill.

No usable connection: the pairing code was refused, or the connection expired, was
replaced or reached its delivery limit. The user selects Connect Claude for a fresh code.
The wallet is in the middle of another action. Retryable with identical input.
A different proposal from this session is still waiting for the user in the wallet.
The wallet refused the proposal's content. Reconnecting does not help.

A file name that is not a plain relative path inside the published directory: a `..` or
`.` component, an absolute path, a separator other than `/`, a symlink or a non-file.
The Wasm's SHA-256 is not the BuildManifest's `wasm_hash`, or not the directory's name.

The BuildManifest does not describe the supplied spec, crate source or lockfile, or is
not a BuildManifest of the current schema.

The published index does not list exactly the directory's files with their SHA-256, or
the directory is not the layout `publish-artifact` writes.

The destination already holds a published directory for this Wasm hash with other
content. Publishing identical content again succeeds.

InstallOperation.description: The only account operation represented by a prepared install intent.

InstallPolicy.description: One address and its value in the account's `Map<Address, Val>` policy argument.

address.description: The exact deployed address from that binding.

policy_index.description: Position in the selected PolicySpec rule and its PolicyBindingSet.

InstallPolicyParams.description:
Account-install arguments for the policy kinds this toolkit composes. The assembler
encodes `Generated` as the generated policy's ignored `u32` value `0`. The spending
limit fields encode `SpendingLimitAccountParams` from the reviewed account library.

spending_limit.description: Canonical decimal i128 from the spec's reviewed `limit` parameter.

PolicyAuthorityEvidence.description:
How the state was acquired. Not part of the approval commitment — ledger numbers, TTLs and
endpoint metadata move without any change in authority — but every read was validated
against it (one endpoint ledger: one response, or for more than 200 keys several reporting
the same ledger; requested keys only; complete reconciliation).

evidence_trust.description: `rpc_reported`: as trustworthy as the configured endpoint, no ledger proof.

raw_ordered_entry_digest.description:
Digest of every raw entry the read used (keys, values, TTLs, absences); it moves with
every payment by a classic signer, which is why it is evidence and not the commitment.

source.description: The operator's name for the RPC source; never its URL.

expired_rules.description: Expired rules that would reach a protected surface or the target if revived.

restricted_key_rules.description: Every live rule, in any context, naming one of the restricted keys.

target_rules.description: Other rules on the target the agent cannot use alone: who else can call it.

PolicyAuthorityState.description: The authority-relevant state behind the answer; part of the commitment.

classic_accounts.description: Signing configuration of every classic account the answer consulted.

ordered_state_digest.description:
Canonical hash of the ordered account rules and transitive storage entries, with every
installed policy's observed code hash. TTLs are not in it.

verifiers.description: Code of every verifier the answer consulted.

PolicyCallSurfaceVerdict.description:
Who could change the account, reset the bound policies, or call the new rule's target, at
one observed ledger, for the stated `scope` only. Never a safety verdict, and advisory to
whoever receives it over MCP: the wallet that holds the owner key recomputes it against its
own RPC and accepts only when `refusals` and `unresolved` are both empty and every
`authority_list` entry names at least one identity it trusts (its own keys, or identities
trusted through its protected UI, never one marked `aliases_restricted_key`) (Decision D7).

authority_commitment.description:
Hash of the separate canonical `CommitmentPreimage` in `ozpb-call-surface-core`,
documented in `docs/CANONICAL-HASHING.md`. It includes the registry snapshot root
and each bound policy's address/code observation, not just the verdict's addresses.
The observed ledger and acquisition evidence are excluded. Approval binds to this
hash and the pre-signing re-read recomputes it; it authenticates nothing by itself.

authority_list.description:
Every live rule that can change the account or reach a bound policy, as policy-free
`all_of` requirements over resolved identities, in rule order.

authority_state.description: The authority-relevant state behind the answer (committed).

coverage_exclusions.description: Live rules for other contracts: not analysed.

evidence.description: How the state was acquired (recorded, never compared).

grant.description: The spec rule the answer is about, with its exact `add_context_rule` arguments.

notes.description: Information for the screen; none of it blocks.

refusals.description: Unconditional refusals inside the scope. Trust never overrides one.

scope.description:
What the answer covers: the target(s), the account's management surface and the bound
policies. Never an account-wide "nothing else".

unresolved.description: Evidence gaps inside the scope. Any entry blocks acceptance.

PolicyGrant.description: The rule being installed, as the check read it from the hashed spec.

policies.description: The new rule's `policies` map, in spec order.

signers.description: The new rule's signers: the restricted keys the refusals look for.

stateful.description: The rule keeps state between calls (a counter or a spending window).

target.description: The contract the new `CallContract` rule targets.

PolicyIdentity.description:
A required identity with what a wallet compares against its own keys. One marked
`aliases_restricted_key` must never be counted as an owner.

oneOf.description: An existing classic Stellar account controlled by its master key alone.

A key behind a recognized owner verifier. Match on `scheme` + `public_key` (the
canonical key); the verifier address is only where this account checks it, and the
same key behind another copy of that verifier is the same identity. An ed25519 key here
is also the same identity as a classic account whose master key it is.

public_key.description: Canonical key, hex: 32 bytes for ed25519, the first 65 bytes for WebAuthn.

oneOf.description: A `Default` rule: every call the account authorizes, management included.
`CallContract(account)`: the account's own management methods.
`CallContract(bound policy)`: that policy's install/uninstall, which resets its state.
`CallContract(target)`: a second way to call the new rule's target.

PolicyRequirement.description: Who must sign for the rule to authorize anything.

oneOf.description: A policy-free rule: every one of these must sign.

Every policy is recognized as demanding at least one of the rule's own signers: any
one of these, within those policies' further limits.

usable_alone.description: The restricted keys can use the rule without anyone else.

PolicyRuleEnumerationEvidence.description:
Only complete enumeration strategies can produce a verdict. The reader must verify
the active count and resolve every rule's transitive signer and policy references.

PolicySignerKey.description: A signer exactly as the account stores it.

rule_id.description: `null` when the finding is about the new rule itself; never omitted.

unsupported.description: Which shape this version refuses, on `E_UNSUPPORTED_AUTHORITY`.

oneOf.description:
A policy decides who may act: any policy on a rule that can change the account or reach
a bound policy (a k-of-n threshold, a guarded recovery rule), or an unreadable one.
A contract signer (nested smart account).
An external signer whose verifier is not recognized.
A classic account with other signers or thresholds the master key cannot meet.
A classic account that does not exist, so cannot authenticate now.
Key data a recognized verifier can never accept.

PolicyVerifierObservation.description:
The code observed at a verifier, and its scheme when that code is a recognized owner
verifier.

account_contract.description: The smart-account contract on which `add_context_rule` is invoked.

authority.description:
The live authority answer these arguments were checked against; its
`authority_commitment` covers them.

context_contract.description: The contract named by the new rule's `CallContract` context.

delegate_signers.description:
The account's typed signer arguments for `add_context_rule`, in the same shape the
authority answer reports them.

policies.description:
One entry per policy in the selected spec rule. The preparer must match each
index and address to the binding set, match the install parameters to the spec,
and reject missing or duplicate indexes and addresses before returning an intent.

valid_until_ledger.description: Explicit `null` means no expiration; omission must not silently grant one.

tools.description: Record an unsigned transaction envelope via simulateTransaction in record mode into a RecordingBundle. Network read through the server's configured RPC source when there is one; the envelope is confidential input.

envelope_xdr_base64.description: Unsigned transaction envelope, base64 XDR. Confidential input (§6.5).

rpc_source.description: As for `record_transaction`: a configured source by name, or the only one when omitted.

tools.name: record_simulation

tools.description: Record an executed Stellar transaction (by hash, via Stellar RPC) into a RecordingBundle: the authorization tree, token movements, and dual hashes. Network read. Reads through the server's configured RPC source when there is one; do not ask the user for an endpoint.

network_passphrase.description:
Network passphrase (e.g. "Test SDF Network ; September 2015"). Taken from the source
when one is used; if given as well, it must be that source's network.

rpc_source.description:
Name of an RPC source the server's operator configured. Omit both this and `rpc_url`
when the server has exactly one source: it is used.

rpc_url.description:
Another RPC endpoint URL instead of a configured source; requires
`network_passphrase`. On the hosted service this must be an allowlisted endpoint.

tools.name: record_transaction

tools.description: Evaluate a PolicySpec with the layer-1 reference suite and return labeled permit/deny evidence and coverage. Pure; does not run contract integration or live preflight.
tools.name: reference_suite

all_agree.description: True iff the original permits and every derived deny-case denies.

coverage.description:
Boundary classes actually exercised, as `"<class>: <count>"`. `all_agree` is silent
about coverage, so this is what says how wide the evidence is.

missing_classes.description:
Classes a rule's shape requires but the suite did not exercise, as
`"rule[<i>]: <class>"`. Checked per rule, so one rule's coverage cannot vouch for
another's gap. Non-empty means the evidence is narrower than `all_agree` implies — a
gate failure, not a warning.

permit_only_classes.description:
Classes exercised but never shown to *deny*, as `"rule[<i>]: <class>"`. Usually a
degenerate bound rather than a gap — a cap of `i128::MAX` cannot be exceeded — so this
is reported, not gated. It means the grant is effectively unbounded on that axis.

report.description: The labeled permit/deny evidence report (layer 1) as JSON.

unmodeled_reviewed_policies.description:
Composed **reviewed** policies (e.g. `oz:spending_limit`) that layer 1 does NOT
model, as `"rule[<i>]: <kind>"`. When non-empty, `all_agree` covers only the
scope+count semantics — the listed policies are enforced on-chain but their stateful
caps/windows are outside this report. Never read `all_agree` as coverage of these.

tools.description: Only after the user's explicit final permission-card confirmation: send existing ozpb-grant-proposal/v1 JSON to the paired local testnet wallet as an unverified draft. Does not deploy, sign, install or approve. The wallet user must review it. Retries of identical bytes are idempotent; do not change bytes to retry an expired/rejected proposal without new confirmation.

proposal_json.description: Existing ozpb-grant-proposal/v1 JSON, at most 16 KiB. Only after final confirmation.

tools.name: send_wallet_proposal

wallet_review_required.description: Delivery is not wallet verification, approval, deployment or installation.

tools.description: Synthesize a minimum-permission PolicySpec from RecordingBundle(s) plus explicit user decisions (signer set, lifetime, widenings). Pure, deterministic, exact-by-default, fail-closed.

account.description:
The account compatibility record as JSON (SmartAccountRecord).

Omit it and synthesis builds it from the same recordings: the address is the selected
authorizer and the code hash is the one observed for it. Nothing is invented — an
account whose code the recordings never observed is still `E_INCOMPATIBLE_ACCOUNT`.

bundles.description: One or more RecordingBundles as JSON.

decisions.description:
The user decisions (UserDecisions) as JSON.

Required, and deliberately: the signer set, the lifetime and the call cap are what the
grant *is*. A default here would mean the toolkit chose how much authority to hand out.

selected_authorizer.description:
The selected smart-account authorizer (strkey).

Omit it and synthesis derives it from the recordings, but only when they leave no
choice to make: exactly one authorizing address that runs observed Wasm. Two such
addresses is a decision about whose account is being constrained, and a caller who
did not state it has not made it — so that is an error naming the candidates rather
than a pick.

signed_registry_snapshot.description:
Signed capability-registry snapshot. Its signature, network, validity window, and
rollback version are verified against the server/CLI-configured trusted root; the
request cannot select its own trust root.

Omit it to use the snapshot the operator configured. Supplying one is still allowed and
still verified against the configured root — a request can bring a newer snapshot, never
a different root.

spending_limit_capability.description:
Reviewed spending-limit wasm hash (hex), if composing it.

[`PINNED_SPENDING_LIMIT`] selects the pinned reviewed policy by name instead of by 64
hex characters. It stays an opt-in rather than becoming a default: composing a reviewed
third-party contract into a grant is a decision, and the tool should not make it because
a spending limit appeared in the decisions.

template_family.description:
Audited template pack to render from. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_FAMILY`], the only
family this milestone registers.

tools.name: synthesize_policy

tools.description: Verify generated non-lock files, Wasm and BuildManifest against a PolicySpec rule, and report offline behavior separately. For an artifact generate_code built in this session, pass its build_manifest_hash as generated_artifact instead of the files. Resource-consuming; live preflight remains separate.

claimed_build_manifest.description: BuildManifest supplied with the artifact. Omission is reported separately.

claimed_generated_files.description:
Every generated file except `Cargo.lock`, as relative path → contents. This is
exactly the set hashed into `source_hash`: it includes `Cargo.toml`,
`rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, and `src/contract.rs`.

The implementation must compare the complete key set as well as contents. A missing
manifest/toolchain file or an extra source module is a mismatch, not reproduction.

claimed_wasm_base64.description: Built artifact to reproduce. Omission is reported as not verified, never success.

generated_artifact.description:
Instead of the three claimed fields: the `build_manifest_hash` that `generate_code`
returned earlier in the same MCP session. That server substitutes the files, Wasm and
manifest it built before anything is checked or hashed, so the request is evaluated
exactly as if they had been sent — without copying a crate and its Wasm through the
conversation. Every other entry point refuses it.

tools.name: verify

models_all_policies.description:
Whether layer 1 models **every** policy composed into this rule. Its own dimension,
deliberately not folded into `matches`: "the reproductions agree" and "the evidence
covers every composed policy" are different claims, and collapsing them would let a
green `matches` imply coverage the report does not have.

unmodeled_reviewed_policies.description:
The composed reviewed policies layer 1 does not model, as `"rule[<i>]: <kind>"`.
Non-empty means those policies are enforced only on-chain.
